name: Talk the Talk
note: UI-24 (owner, 2026-11-19): bowling words and Roguewood's own, each with a drawn picture. Shown from the Clubhouse menu: How to Play, then Talk the Talk. Diagram kinds are drawn by src/presentation/glossary_diagram.gd; rack spots are 1-10, roll 1 pins draw orange and roll 2 blue as in the frame review, an outline is a pin left standing.

terms.text: A themed set of eight Divisions, with its own lanes, rivals and items. Pick one on the League Board.
One go at a League, from Division 1 until you win it or miss a target. Every run is shuffled afresh, so the Pro Shop differs each time.
One of a League's eight stages: an Opener, a Feature and a Boss, in that order.
Reach its target score within two frames to win. Miss the target and the run is over.
A Division's first match: the lowest target, always on House Oil.
The second match, with a higher target. In some Leagues it moves to a special lane.
A Division's last match, against its rival. Their boss rule changes the game; tap the rule badge any time to read it.
The named bowler you face in a boss match. Reach their target to beat them; your first win earns their plaque.
Division 8's boss match. Win it to win the League, and its trophy.
Ten fresh pins and up to two rolls. Each match gives you two frames.
All ten pins down with your first roll. It ends the frame at once, and scores the most.
All ten pins down, using both rolls.
Pins still standing after both rolls. The pins that fell still score, but there is no strike or spare bonus.
The pins still standing after your first roll: what you have left to spare.
A leave with the head pin down and a gap between the pins still standing. Hard to pick up; some Charms pay extra for spares from big leaves.
Two strikes in a row.
Three strikes in a row. Your streak carries from match to match, and any frame that is not a strike ends it.
A roll that drops into a gutter beside the lane and knocks nothing down. A Bumper Guard can bounce it back, once a frame.
The ten pins in their triangle, numbered 1 to 10. Between matches you choose which pin stands on each spot.
Pin 1, at the front of the rack: usually the first pin the ball meets.
The strike spot, between the head pin and the 3 pin if you bowl right-handed (the 2 pin if left-handed). The picture follows your Throw Settings.
The 7 and the 10, at the back corners: the hardest pins to reach.
The four pins at the back of the rack: 7, 8, 9 and 10.
A ball that curves on its way to the pins. Swirl the held ball to charge spin before you flick: more charge, more hook.
Enough spin and a roll counts as curved; otherwise it is straight and goes where you aim. Cards say which they want.
The spin you wind into the held ball by swirling it. A full charge gives the biggest hook.
Lanes are oiled. The ball skids through the oil and hooks once it reaches dry lane. House Oil is the standard pattern; other lanes change it.
The far end of the lane, past the oil, where a hook bites. Dry Backend makes it bite harder.
The lane is 39 narrow boards from gutter to gutter. A board is a small step: Narrow Lane moves each gutter in by two.
The ring at your target shrinks while you hold the ball. Roll through it while it is small: Sweet adds +1 Mult, Perfect +2. Your best roll in a frame counts, once.
Points from pins and cards. Each pin that falls adds its Value: 10 for a Wood pin.
The multiplier. A strike starts at ×4 and a spare at ×2; balls and Charms add to it or multiply it.
When a frame ends, Value × Mult is banked into your match score. A strike with ten Wood pins: (40 + 100) × 4 = 560.
Scores a pin again, as if it fell twice. Only its score repeats, not the crash.
Money a card pays you, on top of your winnings for each match you win. Spend it in the Pro Shop.
Between matches: buy balls, pins, Charms and more, sell what you no longer need, or reroll for new offers.
Your hand. Tap one to throw it; you draw again every frame. The House Ball is always there besides.
Special pins for your rack. Each scores its own way when it falls, or while it stands.
They work on every frame, scoring after the pins, from left to right, so their order matters. Reorder them in the Pro Shop.
One-use cards: each does one thing, once, at the moment its card says.
A ball mod attaches to one of your ball cards; a pin mod goes on a pin in your rack. Either changes how it scores.
Pro Shop improvements kept for the whole run, such as an Extra Shelf of offers.
The pins, ball cards and money a run starts with. Choose one on the League Board; more unlock as you play.
Every item in the game, kept in the Clubhouse: what you have found, and how to unlock the rest.
Challenges, some across your Career and some within one run. Finishing one earns its ribbon and often unlocks an item.
Your Clubhouse shelf: League titles, rivals' plaques and Clubhouse upgrades, each celebrated after the run that earned it.
